properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Anthony's VS Code work log (SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entry [gap] of 2026-10-05, lines 389-398). Asked "how does a hextools PR affect Planrunner?", the reporter's agent traced the path by hand. Expected: "either a cross-design reference edge (member node → member node, resolved through the hub's pins) that blast radius follows, or the radius naming 'stops here: N edges leave this design toward <member>'". Inferred: "the `crosses_published_boundary` flag on rows is the natural place to report the exit."

WHAT IS SETTLED, AND IS NOT OFFERED AS LIVE: an edge from one store to another. dec:nested-graphs (accepted) chose separate graphs linked by MIRRORING, "because an edge cannot cross a store". cap:mirror-surface (verified) is that link: a consumer mirrors the provider's published surface and draws ordinary local edges to it. dec:until-designs-share-a-server-the-cross-design-check-runs-at-the-hub (accepted) says where a check across designs runs. What is open is how to deliver option (b) of dec:idea-a-change-upstream-reaches-the-sibling-that-never-asked: "a change to a provided surface then reaches its consumers through propagation".

THE FINDING THIS ANSWERS: fact:root-cause-a-blast-radius-stops-at-its-design-by-design-and-nothing-says-where-it-left-2026-10-05. With a mirror in place, two radii run by hand give the path across designs. No row says a node belongs to another design, and no skill says to continue.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE ROW SAYS IT IS FOREIGN. An impacted node mirrored from another design carries `mirror_of` (that design's id and name), and the summary adds `leaves_design: [{design, via: [interface ids], count}]`. This is the reporter's "stops here" line, read from the mirror coordinate the consumer already holds. Additive fields only. SIZE: small to moderate.
(b) THE HUB NAMES WHO IS BEYOND. A provider cannot know its consumers (the diamond). A hub can: its pins (external_dependency) and each member's `mirrors()` say who consumes which published interface. A hub-side read maps a member radius's boundary_crossings to the members that mirror them. SIZE: moderate.
(c) A HUB RADIUS THAT CONTINUES. Seed in member A, take the published interfaces it crossed, and continue in each member that mirrors them, starting from the mirrored node. Report per design, each with its own depth bound and truncation. It runs at the hub, per the accepted ruling. SIZE: large.
(d) SKILL ONLY. The impact-check and hub skills teach the two-step chain: a radius in the provider, then a radius seeded at the mirrored interface in each consumer. They also say that a member with no mirror has no path to follow. SIZE: small.
(e) THE HUB HOLDS THE LINK. Record the hand-traced links at the hub, as proposed edges between hub-level stand-ins for member nodes, which is what the reporter offered their user. Member designs stay untouched. But this duplicates what mirroring does, and goes stale silently. SIZE: small to write, costly to keep.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- Every option needs the link to exist first. The reporter's planrunner requirements had no mirror of hextools, so (a) to (c) would have said nothing. The first testable step: does hextools designate its published interfaces, and does planrunner mirror them?
- A mirror is a dated copy. A radius carried through a stale mirror reports yesterday's consumer, so (b) and (c) should report each mirror's age.
- On reflow2's own design a depth-2 radius already reaches about a tenth of the design (fact:release-includes-is-64-percent-of-reflow2s-edges-and-makes-any-blast-radius-around-a-file-about-a-tenth-of-the-design-2026-09-29). Chaining designs multiplies that, so a hub radius must stay a summary by default.
- A hub may not reach a member that is served elsewhere, because a registry-served engine does not reach out. (c) must name each member it could not read, and never answer as if there were none.
- Every option is additive. propagate_from's existing fields and defaults stay as they are ("my brother likes using as is").

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.
properties.name: OPEN — should a blast radius say where it leaves its design (each mirrored node or published interface it reaches, and the design on the other side), and should a hub carry a member's radius into the members that mirror what it reached?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an open question from a field-log [gap] whose cause was measured to be partly by design (dec:nested-graphs) and partly a missing report. Under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed. SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05. Searched first: hubs, mirrors, pair_designs, external_dependency, compose_and_analyse, published surfaces. The idea extends the mirror link, and mints no new one.
